propositions: An errored gold pair is incorrectly counted as a decision flip because the flip computation at parity.py:107 compares decision fields without an errored guard, treating a synthetic error decision as a real model verdict.

A single transient infrastructure event (throttle/timeout) on one arm of a parity run fails the quality gate criterion (b) by fabricating a decision flip, cascading to four gating failures including the never-acceptable criterion.

The parity report cannot distinguish real decision flips from fabricated ones because errored_pairs is not surfaced as a separate metric and the gating-failure string is byte-identical across scenarios with 0/1/3 real flips and 3/2/0 errors respectively.
An errored record with errored=True and valid=True produces a completely silent fabricated flip with no corroborating validity or error-rate signal, undetectable by arm-level metrics.

The defect violates the module contract (parity.py:46) that errored is not a model verdict, and double-counts the same event under both criterion (b) verdict agreement and criterion (d) error-rate gating.
